claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior plastic strain and toughness to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed superiority is governed by enhanced dislocation-mediated plasticity arising from severe lattice distortion in the multi-principal-element solid solution.
Lattice distortion activates multiple slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has a lower effective ductile-to-brittle transition temperature than pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits significant lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
Pure tungsten has limited dislocation mobility and a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten will be compared using tensile and fracture-toughness tests under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed test regime is at temperatures of at least 1000 degrees Celsius with controlled strain rates and plasma-facing loading conditions.
The high concentration of solute atoms and associated lattice distortions create obstacles and sources for dislocation motion, producing enhanced dislocation activity.
Atomic-size mismatch in WTaTiVZr produces significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion facilitates multiple-slip activation and enhanced dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced dislocation mobility delays crack initiation and propagation in WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten tends toward brittle failure because it has fewer available plastic-deformation mechanisms.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, WTaTiVZr will show greater plastic strain to failure and fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The predicted improvement should be accompanied by observable active dislocation-mediated deformation.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply under high-temperature plasma-facing and reactor conditions but may be less pronounced at lower temperatures.
Irradiation may alter the dislocation dynamics responsible for the proposed improvement.
